**What exists now:** \\u0060NodeOwner\\u0060 (the owner\\u0027s id is the daemon\\u0027s OS account name, read in one place and registered in \\u0060DaemonHost\\u0060), and an owner-only rule in \\u0060RequestPrincipal\\u0060 that refuses a mismatched principal header with a 422. \\u0060TriggerDecider.RecordExternalEvent\\u0060 takes a \\u0060Principal\\u0060 and refuses a \\u0060\\u003Cmodule\\u003E/\\u003Cname\\u003E\\u0060 kind to everyone but that module, the owner included. Design doc sections 14.4 and 14.5 state both rules.\\n- **Gotchas:** a call with no header now records under the account name rather than \\u0060owner\\u0060. \\u0060Principal.LocalOwner\\u0060 (\\u0060owner\\u0060) still exists for tests that call services directly, but no source code uses it now. The join task should change only how the \\u0060NodeOwner\\u0060 singleton is built (from the project\\u0027s root record). If the daemon and the CLI run as different accounts, the CLI is refused until then.\\n- **Deliberately left undone:** no change to the CLI, the token middleware, or token resolution, and no member roles or import-time role checks. Those are ruled to land together after phase 3. \\u0060ModuleScope.RequireOwnKind\\u0060 stays in the service, so the existing module messages are unchanged, even though the decider now covers the prefix half
